question: How does Schwab utilize its scale to cheaply acquire new clients and how could Edward Jones replicate a similar strategy?

claims.text: Schwab scale mechanism - The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) lists scale as a key competitive advantage. Schwab says it can spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and use its resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), CEO Rick Wurster said Schwab's sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with Schwab, keeps its cost-to-serve low. He said this lets Schwab invest in client capabilities that fuel growth. He also said that, with nearly $12 trillion in assets and more than 46 million client accounts, doing more for existing clients is as important a source of growth as acquiring new ones.

The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) describes management's approach as coupling Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low, so products are affordable. Schwab calls this part of its "no trade-offs" approach.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said Schwab is using answer engine optimization so it shows up on the AI platforms where investors do research. He said this is already reaching a growing number of clients and that Schwab will do more.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab is simplifying and automating work so people and technology can support more clients. He described the goals as keeping its structural cost advantage, keeping cost to serve low, and creating capacity to reinvest in technology and capabilities.

Schwab's 2Q26 press release (July 2026) reports 1.4 million new brokerage account openings in the quarter, bringing total client accounts to 48.0 million. It also reports core net new assets of $119.8 billion, up 49% versus 2Q25.

Edward Jones on the same dimension, new-client acquisition: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership is making substantial investments in initiatives that include targeting new clients. These are High Net Worth, Workplace (local business owners and their employees), and a new digital platform for Next Generation investors. The filing says their success depends on broad adoption by financial advisors, CSTPs and home office associates, and that the Partnership cannot reliably predict their timing or outcome.

Edward Jones's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-06-27 (published 2025-08-08) shows client households at period end of 6.7 million, up 3%. Net new households were 27,000 for the period versus 60,000 a year earlier (-55%), and 77,000 for the six months versus 124,000 (-38%). Financial advisors at period end were 20,309, up 4%.

Edward Jones's 10-Q for the quarter ended 2025-09-26 (published 2025-11-07) shows client households at period end of 6.7 million, up 3%. Net new households were 24,000 for the period versus 53,000 a year earlier (-55%), and 101,000 for nine months versus 177,000 (-43%). Financial advisors at period end were 20,429, up 3%.

The evidence above only provides objective context for the strategic question asked. Whether or how Edward Jones should act is a judgment for the strategy team to make, beyond the scope of this evidence engine.

adjacent.text: A trade-press article (published 2026-08-20) says Schwab pays W-2 advisors salary and bonus for winning client assets that it largely hands them "on a platter". It also says Schwab's earlier retail hiring push took about five years to reach 3,000 advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative. It describes advisor hiring and lead-handoff, not a disclosed scale-driven acquisition cost.

gaps.what: Schwab does not disclose a cost per acquired client or marketing cost per new account in the evidence. Schwab's cost-to-serve advantage and its account openings are stated, but the link from scale to cheap acquisition is not quantified.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab investor day materials or 10-K disclosure on marketing and acquisition expense; analyst estimates of customer acquisition cost

gaps.what: Edward Jones's cost of acquiring a new client household is not found in the evidence provided. Its net new household figures in the evidence run only through 3Q25, with no figures for 4Q25 to 2Q26.
gaps.suggested_source: Edward Jones 10-K and 10-Q MD&A, including later-quarter net new household data, and earnings or investor materials
